1. admin-user  [access-critical]  fixes SSH-003, USR-003
   Create an admin account with sudo and the keys of an existing account
   create   /etc/sudoers.d/90-stackward-ops (0440)
            checked first with: visudo -c -f <new file>
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/sudoers.d/90-stackward-ops
            @@ -0,0 +1,4 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step admin-user, the admin account.
            +# NOPASSWD because the account has no password; stackward never sets one.
            +# Remove this file to take the rights away.
            +ops ALL=(ALL:ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL
   run      useradd --create-home --home-dir /home/ops --user-group --shell /bin/bash ops
            # create the account with a home and its own group; its password stays locked
   run      install -d -m 0700 -o ops -g ops /home/ops/.ssh
            # create ~/.ssh, owned by the account, mode 0700
   run      install -m 0600 -o ops -g ops /home/ubuntu/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/ops/.ssh/authorized_keys
            # copy the authorized keys of ubuntu on the host, so no key passes through the plan
   note     ops gets sudo without a password (NOPASSWD), like the cloud image's default account; USR-004 lists it. Set a password and drop NOPASSWD later if you prefer.
   note     Prove it before you confirm: open a new SSH session as ops with the key of ubuntu and run sudo stackward confirm from there.
   note     lock-default-user is planned once a session of this account applies it.
   undo     Remove the sudoers drop-in and delete the account ops with its home and group (userdel --remove). Anything saved in that home is deleted with it.
            rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/90-stackward-ops
            userdel --remove ops

2. sshd-hardening  [access-critical]  fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005
   Allow key logins only, refuse root and limit auth tries with an early sshd drop-in
   create   /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf (0644)
            checked first with: sshd -t -f <new file>
            --- /dev/null
            +++ b/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf
            @@ -0,0 +1,6 @@
            +# Written by stackward: plan step sshd-hardening, fixes SSH-001, SSH-003, SSH-005.
            +# Named to sort first: sshd keeps the first value it reads. Remove this
            +# file and reload ssh.service to undo.
            +PasswordAuthentication no
            +PermitRootLogin no
            +MaxAuthTries 3
   run      systemctl try-reload-or-restart ssh.service
            # load the new settings; running sessions stay open
   restarts ssh
   note     sshd runs under socket activation (ssh.socket); the drop-in sets no port or listen address, so reloading ssh.service is enough and ssh.socket is left alone.
   note     Existing SSH sessions stay open. Before you confirm, log in again in a new session with your key: that is the proof the change works.
   note     Ubuntu 22.04 and later and Debian 12 and later; older OpenSSH reads KbdInteractiveAuthentication differently.
   undo     Remove the drop-in and reload ssh.service; the earlier values return for new logins.
            rm -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-stackward-hardening.conf
            systemctl try-reload-or-restart ssh.service
